cite: Katha Upanisad 2.2.13, quoted in BG 2.12 purport
iast: nityo nityānāṁ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṁ yo vidadhāti kāmān / tam ātma-sthaṁ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṁ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām
translation: Of all eternals He is the one chief eternal, of all conscious beings the one chief conscious being, and He alone fulfils the desires of the many. The sober who see Him within themselves attain eternal peace, not others. (plain rendering of the verse Prabhupada quotes; his purport follows)

cite: Katha Upanisad 1.2.18, quoted in BG 2.20 purport
iast: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin nāyaṁ kutaścin na babhūva kaścit / ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṁ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
translation: The knowing soul is never born and never dies; it has not come from anything and nothing has come from it. Unborn, eternal, ever-existing, ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain. (plain rendering; Prabhupada notes it is the same teaching as BG 2.20 and that vipascit marks the soul as full of consciousness)

iast: om pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idaṁ pūrṇāt pūrṇam udacyate / pūrṇasya pūrṇam ādāya pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate
translation: The Personality of Godhead is perfect and complete, and because He is completely perfect, all emanations from Him, such as this phenomenal world, are perfectly equipped as complete wholes. Whatever is produced of the Complete Whole is also complete in itself. Because He is the Complete Whole, even though so many complete units emanate from Him, He remains the complete balance. (Prabhupada, Sri Isopanisad)

iast: īśāvāsyam idaṁ sarvaṁ yat kiñca jagatyāṁ jagat / tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā mā gṛdhaḥ kasya svid dhanam
translation: Everything animate or inanimate that is within the universe is controlled and owned by the Lord. One should therefore accept only those things necessary for himself, which are set aside as his quota, and one should not accept other things, knowing well to whom they belong. (Prabhupada, Sri Isopanisad)

iast: hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṁ mukham / tat tvaṁ pūṣann apāvṛṇu satya-dharmāya dṛṣṭaye
translation: O my Lord, sustainer of all that lives, Your real face is covered by Your dazzling effulgence. Kindly remove that covering and exhibit Yourself to Your pure devotee. (Prabhupada, Sri Isopanisad)

cite: Svetasvatara Upanisad 6.23, quoted in SB 2.9.43 purport
iast: yasya deve parā bhaktir yathā deve tathā gurau / tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ
translation: Only unto one who has unflinching devotion to the Lord and to the spiritual master does transcendental knowledge become automatically revealed. (Prabhupada's translation in the purport; also quoted in SB 4.28.65 purport)

cite: Katha Upanisad 1.2.23 / Mundaka 3.2.3, quoted in CC Madhya 6.87 purport
iast: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena / yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṁ svām
translation: The Self is not attained by instruction, by intelligence, or by much hearing; He is attained by the one whom He Himself chooses, to whom He reveals His own form. (plain rendering of the verse Prabhupada quotes there)

cite: Brhan-naradiya Purana, quoted at CC Adi 17.21
iast: harer nāma harer nāma harer nāmaiva kevalam / kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva nāsty eva gatir anyathā
translation: In this Age of Kali there is no other means, no other means, no other means for self-realization than chanting the holy name, chanting the holy name, chanting the holy name of Lord Hari. (Prabhupada)
